posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
Edmund has some new beamsplitters. I'm not familiar with them, but they look interesting. I would have provided a link to Edmund, but their site seems to be down this morning.

They are called "polarizing plate beamsplitters."

"These polarizers consist of a thin layer of aluminum MicroWires adhered to a glass window....When incident light strikes the grid, P-polarized light contacts a dielectric and is transmitted while S-polarized light contacts a mirror and is reflected...."

The wavelength range is 420 to 670nm, the transmission in this range for P-polarized light is between ~85 to 88%, and the reflection of S-polarized light is about the same. The stock number is C48-544, price $95.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md: It's also got an AR coating on the back that they say reflects only 0.8%

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md: Doing some more browsing of the catalog, I also noted a digital micrometer by Mitutoyo, C54-878, that has 1 micron resolution and LCD readout, for only $143. This is far superior to the El Cheapo variety from Harbor Freight, which has much less resolution and a clunky non-LCD readout.

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md: I did some more checking on micrometers with 1-micron resolution and a LCD display. It seems they are offered by a variety of manufacturers, including Mitutoyo, in the $80 to $90 price range. Once again, Edmund proves to be almost unreasonably expensive!

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Joe, my favorite is a Mititoyo with .0005" resolution over 6" and was only about $120 15 years ago. It has a feature called "Absolute" which is very convenient. It allows you to turn on the caliper in any location and get a good reading. The other option is you must turn it on at 0 each time.
